h1: Veravian Resort (Wang Nam Khiao) — a hillside resort selling Khao Phaeng Ma views and cool mountain air
intro: If Wang Nam Khiao brings to mind a resort on a high hillside, cool air, and a pool that looks out onto a mountain backdrop — Veravian Resort, known in Thai as Veravian Resort (Wela Wian), is one of the names travellers in this area have talked about for years · it is a Modern-Green resort set on a hillside around 550 metres above sea level, right next to Khao Phaeng Ma, a spot many know for its wild gaur and lush green mountain views · the main draw is the infinity pool at the centre of the resort that blends into the mountain view with no visible edge, private pool villas, and the family-friendly V Play zone with a mini-zoo and playground · from about ฿4,600/night for a room with a pool, with options ranging from budget capsule rooms up to a two-bedroom pool villa · but in the spirit of a friend telling a friend, this place has both praise and gripes worth knowing before you book.

body.html: Who Veravian Resort is for, in a nutshell — if we had to sum it up in one line, Veravian Resort is for people who come to Wang Nam Khiao to "be with the view and the cool air" more than for flawless luxury · the resort sits on a hillside around 550 metres up, right next to Khao Phaeng Ma in Wang Nam Khiao subdistrict, Wang Nam Khiao district, Nakhon Ratchasima · it has been open since 2010 and had a major renovation in 2023, which is why some zones clearly look newer than others · the concept here is a Modern-Green Resort that leans into harmony with nature, with several room zones to choose from, from budget capsule rooms up to a two-bedroom pool villa with a private pool · real reviews line up on who fits best here: families with young children, couples who want a private pool, and groups of friends coming to relax and shoot photos against the mountain view · those expecting a flawless five-star hotel in every corner or full luxury-resort service may need to adjust their expectations, because this is a mid-sized resort built mainly around atmosphere and location · for context, TripAdvisor ranks it #2 of 17 specialty lodging properties in Wang Nam Khiao, which still puts it near the top of the area.

Location and getting there — Veravian Resort is in Moo 15, Pong Talong subdistrict (the Pho Thong Phatthana side), Wang Nam Khiao district, an area known for cool air and ozone quality that ranks among the best in Thailand · the draw of the location is that it sits on a hillside around 550 metres up, right next to Khao Phaeng Ma, giving you a full mountain view and pleasantly cool air for most of the year, especially in the late-rainy-to-early-cool season when there is often light morning mist · from Bangkok it is about a 3-hour drive, passing through Pak Chong–Khao Yai before turning into Wang Nam Khiao · one thing to be clear about is that you really do need your own car here, because the resort is on a hillside in an area with almost no public transport, no Grab, and shops are not within walking distance · some sections of the road up the hill are fairly steep and narrow; an ordinary sedan can make it but you should drive carefully, especially on rainy days when the road is slippery · popular nearby spots like Khao Phaeng Ma (for the gaur), vineyards, hillside cafes, and Wang Nam Khiao market all require a drive, which is just the nature of staying in this area.

"The view from the pool is gorgeous — in the morning there's mist drifting over the mountains, and sipping coffee by the pool is genuinely blissful · the kids loved the mini-zoo and playground, they could play all day without getting bored."

Room types and decor — Veravian splits its rooms into several zones with names that play on the word "time," in keeping with the resort's concept · it starts with the most budget-friendly, Time Village capsule-style rooms (around 30 sqm in the zone), suited to those on a tight budget or coming as a group · stepping up is Second Deluxe, a room style built into the hillside with a sitting balcony · Moment Pool Access, a room that opens straight onto the pool, with a bunk-bed option for families · Minute Suite, a suite with a private pool designed to blend into the mountains · up to Hour Pool Villa, a villa with a private 3×5 metre pool, available in upper-level and lower-level styles, and Family Pool House, a two-bedroom unit with a large pool for families · the design is modern-loft style, playing with bare concrete and warm-toned oak for a clean, understated look · many reviews praise the pool villas as spacious, with private pools that actually get used, and lovely views from the rooms · but to be straight about it, a fair number of reviews note that rooms in some zones are starting to show their age and aren't maintained evenly, especially the capsule rooms, which many say are too small, with little space for luggage, and in some units the bathroom and shower are outside the room itself — so read the room details carefully before booking.

Facilities, pool, and activities — the most talked-about highlight at Veravian is the infinity pool at the centre of the resort, designed so the pool edge appears to flow into the Khao Phaeng Ma mountain view with no visible rim · misty mornings and sunset evenings are the popular times for guests to come up to take photos and chill by the pool · besides the central pool, the pool villa rooms also have a private pool right outside · another spot families love is V Play, the mini-zoo and playground zone, with small animals for kids to feed, wooden play equipment, and activities like a zipline and a maze, giving kids plenty to do all day · there is The Clockwise restaurant with panoramic-view seating, and the Veravian cafe with drinks and homemade bakery · plus a massage room, a nature trail, free Wi-Fi, and free parking · one thing to keep in mind is that the central pool and most villa pools have no heating, so during the cold season when Wang Nam Khiao gets really cold, the pool water becomes too cold to swim in comfortably — better for dipping your feet and taking photos than for serious swimming.

Food and cafe — the resort's main restaurant is The Clockwise Restaurant, which serves food with a mountain view · reviews on the food lean fairly positive, with many praising it as tasty, reasonably priced, with fresh organic vegetables and mushrooms, which fits the Green concept here · breakfast is included in most room packages and earns praise for its freshness and flavour · there is also the Veravian Cafe with coffee, drinks, and freshly baked bakery to enjoy with the view in the late morning · because the resort is on a hillside with no shops within walking distance, having an in-house restaurant and cafe helps a lot, especially for dinner — if you don't feel like driving down the hill to find a restaurant outside, you can just eat at the resort · that said, the in-resort menu isn't as varied as restaurants in town, so if you're staying several nights and want a change of scene, plan to drive out to some of the well-known spots in the Wang Nam Khiao or Khao Yai area.

Service — service is where the reviews are fairly split · the praising side says the staff are friendly, help recommend nearby attractions, and look after the kids' activities well · but there's a fair amount of criticism too, especially around consistency of service and room management — some reviews describe a long wait after check-in because the pool or room wasn't ready yet, and a few ran into issues with room allocation and booking conditions that weren't communicated clearly · this is where it differs from resorts that focus on high-end service, and it's one reason the overall score here isn't sky-high · the advice is to confirm the room details and check-in time with the resort in advance, especially if you've booked a room with a pool or are coming during a long-weekend holiday when it's busy.

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — pulling from Trip.com, TripAdvisor, and Thai reviews like Wongnai, the picture is clearly mixed · on the praise side: the mountain view from the infinity pool is beautiful and photogenic, the cool air is just the nature of the Wang Nam Khiao area, the V Play mini-zoo and playground that kids love, the spacious private pool villas that actually get used, and the tasty food made with fresh organic ingredients · on the watch-out side: the most talked-about issue is cleanliness and upkeep — some reviews found towels in poor condition, bathroom floors that weren't clean, or spots around the resort needing urgent attention · next is hot water that runs inconsistently or comes out cold in several room types, capsule rooms that are small and which many feel aren't worth the price, generator noise near the rooms in some spots, and some of the landscaping plants looking dry and neglected · these gripes don't happen to everyone or every room, but they're worth knowing and choosing your room carefully before booking, because the experience depends quite a bit on the zone and the time you visit.

"The pool villa is spacious, great view, the private pool is fun · but the downside is the hot water doesn't run very strongly, and I wish they'd keep things cleaner · next time I'll pick a recently renovated zone instead."

Price and value comparison — Veravian's prices spread fairly widely by zone · the Time Village capsule rooms start in the low thousands per night, good for budget travellers · rooms with a pool like Moment Pool Access and Minute Suite start from about ฿4,600/night and up · the Hour Pool Villa and two-bedroom Family Pool House move up into several thousand to the low five figures depending on pool size and timing, especially in the cold season (November–January), which is Wang Nam Khiao's peak when prices climb fast · compared with other pool villas in the Khao Yai–Wang Nam Khiao area, Veravian sits in the mid-price group that mainly sells the mountain view and the infinity pool · so value depends on what you weight — if your priorities are the view, cool air, a private pool, and kids' activities, this place delivers at an accessible price · but if you expect flawless rooms and premium-level service, you may feel the price doesn't quite match the condition in some zones, which is why you should pick a recently renovated zone and read the latest reviews before booking.

Things to know before you book — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · one, you definitely need your own car, because the resort is on a hillside with no public transport or Grab, and some stretches of the road up are steep — drive carefully, especially on rainy days · two, pick a room zone that matches your needs — want a private pool, choose a Pool Villa or Minute Suite; coming as a family, choose the Family Pool House; the Time Village capsule rooms suit those on a tight budget but you have to accept the small space and that some units have the bathroom outside the room · three, confirm the hot water and room readiness with the resort in advance, since that's a frequent complaint in reviews · four, if you come in the cold season, be prepared that the pool isn't heated and the water will be very cold, and book ahead because Wang Nam Khiao fills up fast at peak · five, choose free cancellation to be safe if your plans aren't firm, and compare prices across platforms since they shift with the season.

Bottom line — from all the real reviews, Veravian Resort is the best fit for families and couples who come to Wang Nam Khiao for the mountain view, cool air, a private pool, and kids' activities, on an accessible budget · the infinity pool with Khao Phaeng Ma views, the V Play mini-zoo, and the food made with fresh ingredients are the points people consistently praise · but you have to understand, honestly, that this is a mid-sized resort that has been open since 2010, some zones are starting to show their age, and review feedback on cleanliness, hot water, and consistency of service is still something to factor in · if you're after flawless luxury or want to stay without a car, this may not be the answer · but if your priorities are a hillside location with a great view, a natural setting, and activities the whole family can enjoy — and you pick a well-kept zone and set your expectations right — Veravian is still a choice many people come back to in the Wang Nam Khiao area.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Veravian Resort (Wang Nam Khiao)

faq.q: Where is Veravian Resort and how do you get there?
faq.a: It is in Moo 15, Pho Thong Phatthana subdistrict, Wang Nam Khiao district, Nakhon Ratchasima, on a hillside around 550 metres up next to Khao Phaeng Ma · from Bangkok it is about a 3-hour drive through Pak Chong–Khao Yai · note that you need your own car, since there is no public transport or Grab, and some stretches of the road up the hill are steep and narrow.

faq.q: What is Veravian Resort's starting price and what room types are there?
faq.a: Time Village capsule rooms start in the low thousands · rooms with a pool like Moment Pool Access and Minute Suite start from about ฿4,600/night · the Hour Pool Villa and two-bedroom Family Pool House move up into several thousand to the low five figures depending on pool size and timing · the cold season (Nov–Jan) is peak, when prices rise fast, so compare several platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Veravian Resort best suited to?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families with young children, couples who want a private pool, and groups of friends coming to relax and shoot photos against the mountain view · there's an infinity pool with Khao Phaeng Ma views and the V Play mini-zoo and playground · it's less suited to those expecting flawless luxury, or to anyone without their own car.

faq.q: What is the pool like at Veravian, and is it heated?
faq.a: There is an infinity pool at the centre of the resort looking out over Khao Phaeng Ma with no visible edge, and the pool villa rooms also have a private pool right outside · note that most pools are not heated, so during the cold season when Wang Nam Khiao gets really chilly the water will be very cold — better for dipping your feet and taking photos than for serious swimming.

faq.q: What do reviews of Veravian Resort criticise?
faq.a: Real reviews are fairly mixed · the most frequent gripe is cleanliness and upkeep in some spots being inconsistent, such as towels in poor condition or bathroom floors that aren't clean, followed by hot water that runs weak or comes out cold, and capsule rooms small enough that many feel they aren't worth the price · pick a recently renovated zone and read the latest reviews before booking.

faq.q: Does Veravian Resort have activities for kids?
faq.a: Yes · the highlight for families is V Play, the mini-zoo and playground zone, with small animals for kids to feed, wooden play equipment, and activities like a zipline and a maze · many reviews say kids can play all day without getting bored, which is what makes the resort a good fit for family trips.
